answer.diagnosis: Every structured first-layer unit has a sharp, fixed 4x4 patch at the exact image centre (rows 10-13, cols 10-13). This patch carries some of each unit's largest-magnitude weights, and its sign is the opposite of what the unit's size template would predict. The blob-coverage units (0, 1, 8, 18, 19, 20, 22, 29) have positive weights on a large disk of radius about 6 and push toward 'large'. Yet on this patch their weights are strongly negative (down to -76). The inverse units (14, 15, 23, 27) are positive on the background, negative on the annulus, and push toward 'small' through layer-2 units u1, u6 and u9. On the same patch their weights are strongly positive (up to 99). A genuine blob-size template should put roughly zero weight on pixels that both small and large blobs always cover. The patch also has crisp edges and sits at a fixed position, while the blobs only lie near the centre. So the model appears to read the intensity of a fixed central square (bright means small, dark means large) as a cue separate from blob size. I also saw scattered strong single background pixels that are consistent across units. These are not coherent, so I attribute them to shared overfitting and leave them alone. Fix: zero the central-patch weights in these 12 units. Then shift each bias by patch sum x (W1 scale / b1 scale) x 0.9, which preserves activations for a bright blob centre (assumed intensity about 0.9). The annulus and background size templates are untouched.
